- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.23 or high positive sentiment) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.11 or below) — adjust upward slightly to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Avoid long-term overconfidence in upward trends — cap 30-day forecasts at 10–15% above recent 18-day average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Correct for lagged price reactions — if sentiment turns positive after a dip, forecast should rise faster than historical pattern suggests.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, reduce forecast volatility — avoid sharp swings in 30-day projections unless accompanied by strong bullish sentiment.
- Apply mean reversion bias correction: if forecast is >15% above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
